newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel-German economy not lowering budget burdens.
newsitem.headline: Waigel-German economy not lowering budget burdens.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Thursday that the nation's economy was not helping to lower budget burdens and unemployment this year would total 4.3 million before falling in 1998.
Waigel was speaking at a press conference where he discussed Germany's attempts to improve its financial position and qualify for European moentary union.
Germany's economy has been turning in sluggish growth in recent quarters, hurting tax revenues and forcing up government spending for unemployment benefits.
Waigel told journalists that such unemployment outlays could cost the government an additional 20 billion marks in 1997.

"Due to uenmployemnt in 1997, it is conceiveable that the government could be forced to pay out an additional 20 billion marks in 1997," Waigel said. "The economy is not helping to lower the budget burdens."
